lessons.title: Introduction to Trees

content.title: What is a Tree?
content.text: A tree is a hierarchical data structure made up of nodes connected by edges. Unlike a linear structure such as an array, a tree represents relationships in levels.

content.title: Root
content.text: The root is the topmost node of a tree. A tree normally has one root node.

content.title: Parent and Child
content.text: A node directly connected above another node is its parent. The node below it is its child.

content.title: Leaf Node
content.text: A leaf is a node that has no children.

content.title: Simple Tree
content.code:
A
       / \
      B   C
     / \
    D   E

A = root
B and C = children of A
D and E = children of B
C, D and E = leaf nodes

key_points: Trees represent hierarchical relationships.
The root is the topmost node.
Nodes can have parents and children.
Leaf nodes have no children.

lessons.title: Tree Terminology

content.title: Depth
content.text: The depth of a node represents the number of edges from the root to that node.

content.title: Height
content.text: The height of a node is the number of edges on the longest path from that node to a leaf. The height of the tree is the height of its root.

content.title: Subtree
content.text: A subtree consists of a node and all of its descendants.

content.title: Degree
content.text: The degree of a node is the number of children it has.

content.title: Example
content.code:
A
       / \
      B   C
     /
    D

Depth(A) = 0
Depth(B) = 1
Depth(D) = 2

key_points: Depth measures distance from the root.
Height measures the longest downward path.
A subtree contains a node and its descendants.
Degree represents the number of children.

lessons.title: Binary Trees

content.title: Binary Tree
content.text: A binary tree is a tree in which each node can have at most two children, commonly called the left child and right child.

content.title: Full Binary Tree
content.text: A full binary tree is a binary tree in which every node has either zero or two children.

content.title: Complete Binary Tree
content.text: A complete binary tree has all levels completely filled except possibly the last, and nodes in the last level are filled from left to right.

key_points: Binary tree nodes have at most two children.
Children are called left and right.
Full and complete describe different structural properties.

lessons.title: Tree Traversal

content.title: Tree Traversal
content.text: Traversal means visiting every node in a tree according to a particular order.

content.title: Preorder
content.text: Preorder visits the current node first, then the left subtree, then the right subtree.

content.title: Preorder
content.code:
A
       / \
      B   C

Preorder: A B C

content.title: Inorder
content.text: Inorder visits the left subtree first, then the current node, then the right subtree.

content.title: Inorder
content.code:
A
       / \
      B   C

Inorder: B A C

content.title: Postorder
content.text: Postorder visits the left subtree, then the right subtree, and finally the current node.

content.title: Postorder
content.code:
A
       / \
      B   C

Postorder: B C A

key_points: Preorder: Root, Left, Right.
Inorder: Left, Root, Right.
Postorder: Left, Right, Root.
Traversal is used to process every node.

lessons.title: Binary Search Trees

content.title: Binary Search Tree
content.text: A binary search tree is a binary tree where values smaller than a node are stored in its left subtree and values larger than the node are stored in its right subtree.

content.title: Searching
content.text: To search for a value, compare it with the current node. If the target is smaller, move left. If larger, move right.

content.title: Insertion
content.text: A new value is inserted by following the same comparison process until an empty position is found.

content.title: Search Example
content.code:
Search for 60:
50 -> target is larger -> right
70 -> target is smaller -> left
60 -> found

key_points: BSTs maintain an ordering property.
Smaller values go left.
Larger values go right.
Searching follows the ordering property.

lessons.title: BST Operations and Complexity

content.title: BST Search
content.text: In a balanced binary search tree, search can take O(log n) time because each comparison eliminates a large portion of the remaining tree.

content.title: Worst Case
content.text: If a BST becomes highly unbalanced, it can behave like a linked list and search, insertion or deletion can degrade to O(n).

content.title: Balanced Trees
content.text: Balanced tree structures try to keep the height relatively small so that operations remain efficient.

key_points: Balanced BST operations can be O(log n).
A badly unbalanced BST can degrade to O(n).
Tree height strongly affects performance.

lessons.title: Tree Implementations

content.title: Tree Node
content.text: A binary tree node commonly stores a value and references to a left child and a right child.

content.title: Python Node
Recursive Traversal
content.text: Tree traversal is naturally expressed using recursion because each subtree is itself a tree.

content.title: Inorder Traversal

key_points: Nodes store values and child references.
Binary nodes commonly have left and right references.
Recursion is commonly used for tree traversal.

lessons.title: Applications of Trees

content.title: File Systems
content.text: Folders and files naturally form hierarchical structures that can be represented using trees.

content.title: Decision Trees
content.text: Decision trees represent decisions as nodes and possible outcomes as branches.

content.title: Expression Trees
content.text: Expression trees can represent mathematical expressions, with operators as internal nodes and values as leaves.

content.title: Why Trees Matter
content.text: Trees are useful whenever information has a hierarchy or when efficient searching and organization are required.

key_points: Trees represent hierarchical information.
File systems are naturally hierarchical.
Decision trees represent choices and outcomes.
Trees are useful for searching and organization.
